sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: A sample of 5 values is: 18, 23, 19, 22, 22. What is the range of this data set?
A data set has 4 values: 10, 10, 12, 12. What is the new mean if an outlier of 34 is added to the data set, making 5 values in all?
A data set is: 22, 11, 12, 20, 20, with a mean of 17. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 48 and 64. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 4. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 3 times the MAD
6 times the MAD
4 times the MAD
16 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 26, 31, 33, 36, 14. Sample B: 39, 29, 38, 35, 49. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Both samples have the same mean.
Sample A, with a mean of 28 compared to 38.
Sample B, with a mean of 28 compared to 38.
Sample B, with a mean of 38 compared to 28.

items.prompt: Sample A: 22, 18, 22, 22, 18. Sample B: 8, 31, 17, 8, 35. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample A, with a range of 27 compared to 4.
Sample B, with a range of 27 compared to 4.
Sample A, with a range of 4 compared to 27.
Both samples have the same range.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 1090 commuters on a train line. She randomly selects 42 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: The researcher's own estimate
The 42 randomly selected commuters on a train line
Only the first 42 commuters on a train line on a list
All 1090 commuters on a train line

items.prompt: A student posts an online form, and 38 students at Lincoln Middle School choose to respond. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 28 shoppers at a grocery store, 9 preferred a new park design. Based on this sample, about how many of the 308 shoppers at a grocery store would you expect to prefer a new park design?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 24, 19, 19, 14, 24. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 2751 shoppers at a grocery store. Student A takes a random sample of 15. Student B takes a random sample of 69. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.
Student A's sample of 15, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Student B's sample of 69, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.

items.prompt: A student surveys 36 shoppers at a grocery store using a convenience sample of her classmates only and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 792 shoppers at a grocery store?
choices: No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.
Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
